name: use-html-theme
description: Themed-HTML toolkit, three pure skills sharing one context-triage preflight. use-html-theme: on any HTML-generation request, offer a catalog of visual themes (Birchline warm-editorial, Technical-minimal docs-site, High-contrast-dark dashboard), apply the chosen theme to all subsequent HTML in the session, and optionally persist it per-project — natural language and [theme: x] inline-flag control, side-by-side preview on request. html-codesign: interactive 'pick and export' decision pages — every question opens with a collapsible context-and-recommendation preamble (free-form rich content on a clarity scaffold), the reader answers, skips, or raises a question on each section, folds answered sections to dense summary rows for review, then exports the decision as Markdown/JSON (slim by default, full ADR-style by toggle) with stable IDs for diffable iteration. html-explain: read-only explainer pages for settled material — authoring maps which parts are intrinsically hardest and budgets the page around them, then enriches with diagrams, annotated figures, build-up sequences, and manipulable widgets ONLY where comprehension actually breaks; clarity canon (Mayer, Sweller, Minto, Heath, Tufte, Bertin, Cleveland) carried as advisory aids, with a standalone encoding fallback for surfaces where the bundled dataviz skill does not exist. Both page skills read recent context and ALWAYS confirm before generating — codesign for unanswered questions, explain for settled work — and hand off to each other when triage disagrees with the request. Portable across Claude Code and Codex.
